conventions.convention: Bosonic sectors are indexed by n ≥ 0, with vacuum sector C. The number operator has domain Σ n²‖Ψ_n‖² < ∞ and multiplies sector n by n; E_N(B) retains precisely the integer-labelled sectors in B.
Countable Choice is assumed. Fock pairings are linear in the second variable; the adjoint definition from the first-variable-linear supplier is transferred by conjugation.

Spacetime signature is (−,+,+,+), while energy-momentum contraction uses its negative (+,−,−,−). Massive current legs have positive energies, positive rest energies, subluminal velocities and balanced signed charges. Cutoffs satisfy 0 < λ < Λ < ∞ and are energies in joules.

Polarization frames are measurable real orthonormal transverse frames almost everywhere. Counting probabilities use a separately constructed finite two-outcome projective instrument for each singleton count event. The zero-count formula uses 0⁰ = 1.

The coherent preparation and Born interpretation are adopted model assumptions. The conclusions concern a prepared positive free-photon state, with conditional draft mathematical suppliers; they assert neither interacting-QED emission nor detector realization.

The magnetic-moment ratio is a source-reported estimate with stated 1σ uncertainty 1.3 × 10⁻¹³, nearby-field cavity correlations, and unreconstructed raw trials, covariance and weights. No independence, posterior or coverage interpretation is added.
The anomaly estimate is the reported ratio minus the exact dimensionless reference 1; this affine translation preserves its deviation, uncertainty and empirical qualifications.

load_bearing.statement: D(N) = {Ψ ∈ F_s(H): Σ n²‖Ψ_n‖² < ∞}, (NΨ)_n = nΨ_n; E_N(B)Ψ = (1_B(n)Ψ_n) and P_n = E_N({n}). These are candidate operators and projections, with well-definedness discharged by the following theorem.

Assume Countable Choice. For a complex Hilbert space H, N is self-adjoint on its stated domain and E_N is a projection-valued measure on the Borel subsets of R, retaining exactly the integer-labelled sectors. Every finite Borel partition gives mutually orthogonal projections summing to the identity.

Under Countable Choice, the stated balanced massive prescribed current, measurable transverse polarizations, finite positive energy cutoffs, constructed coherent preparation and adopted free-photon/Born model, p_n = exp(−Nγ)Nγⁿ/n!, where Nγ = C log(Λ/λ), with 0⁰ = 1. The mean count is Nγ and mean energy is C(Λ−λ). If C > 0 there is no Fock-norm or projective-ray limit as λ decreases to zero, despite bounded mean energy. For the stated one-charge rest-to-velocity current, C(v) = (α/π)(v⁻¹ log((1+v)/(1−v))−2) > 0 for 0 < v < 1.

The authors report −μ/μ_B = g/2 = 1.00115965218059(13), obtained from eleven weighted corrected determinations, with stated 1σ uncertainty 1.3 × 10⁻¹³ and the recorded apparatus, correction, correlation and omitted-data qualifications.

published_dependencies.used_for: Exact countable-choice assumption carried by the Fock, measure and instrument constructions.
Orthogonal projection values, normalization, intersection law and strong countable additivity checked in the local counting-PVM theorem.
Operator equality includes domain equality; the number operator is specified on its maximal square-summability domain.
Adjoint-domain characterization, explicitly transferred to the second-variable-linear Fock convention.
Self-adjointness requires equality of operator values and domains.
Cutoff logarithms, positivity of log 2, and the one-charge angular integral and positivity calculation.
The mathematical soft-current supplier constructs separability from real scalar L² density, then complexifies, takes three components and projects transversely.
Finite-product countability in that explicit separability construction.
Enumeration and countability of nonempty images in the separability construction; its nonempty hypothesis is retained.
Exact meaning of the separability hypothesis required by the Segal–Weyl supplier.
Identification of the sphere measure used in angular norms with polar surface measure.
Energy-to-wave-vector dilation, including preservation of null sets and well-defined composition on completed-measurable L² classes.
Inherited SI normalization, including measured rather than exact μ₀ and ε₀ = (μ₀c²)⁻¹.
The free-photon postulate adopts only its smooth source-free classical input; this does not construct the quantum representation.

concerns.concern: F1 attributes “g_em² = 4πα with g_em > 0” to def-qft-example-data, whose Definition instead introduces the positive coupling named g. The consumed physics theorem allows either sign of g_em and handles this explicitly in proof step 3.1. The example's count and energy calculations remain valid, but F1 should use the supplier's name g or explicitly choose g_em = g.

seams_checked.note: The consumer adopts the same positive transverse Fock space and free Hamiltonian, carries the physical measurement assumptions and conditional supplier status, and makes no interacting-QED or apparatus-realization claim.

The mathematical supplier gives norm, unitary conversion, coherent-sector weights and energy expectation, without physical probabilities. The consumer adds its finite Born instrument, proves the measurable polarization identification, and handles the amplitude sign through σⁿ. Its infrared conclusion is proved independently from overlaps.

The examples-page experiment uses the ideal stable linear Penning invariant only as an operational supplier and explicitly distinguishes the source's additional corrections. The deterministic ratio bound is not used as a statistical uncertainty theorem. Source reporting was checked against https://arxiv.org/html/2209.13084v2, equations (3)–(6), the spectroscopy and cavity paragraphs, and Table 1.

The observable-types supplier distinguishes exact finite-regulator data, formal coefficient records and qualified empirical estimates. The experiment preserves the empirical-estimate classification; the infinite-dimensional coherent construction separately uses the constructed-model postulate and does not claim that the finite-matrix definition covers its Fock space.
